chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had dirhams as a debt upon another man, so he sold wine or pigs while he (the creditor) was watching, and he paid him off. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. As for the creditor, it is permissible, and as for the seller, it is prohibited.'
ai.seo_question: Is money earned from selling wine or pigs permissible for the creditor to keep as debt repayment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the impurity of the source funds does not transfer to the creditor, rendering the debt repayment valid and permissible for him to use. However, for the debtor who sold the impure goods specifically to settle the debt, the money remains prohibited, illustrating the Shia principle that the permissibility of an item can depend on the context of its acquisition and the status of the recipient. This distinction highlights the practical application of *taharah* (purity) in financial transactions within Shia jurisprudence.
